title: Keep them (John 17:6–19)
hookLine: he prays for his friends: not out of the world, but kept from evil
carry: in the world, but not of it
tomorrow: that they may all be one

lines: THE DISCIPLES HEAR IT AT THE TABLE.
cards: If you've ever overheard someone praying for you, you know it's a strange and tender thing. A grandmother at the kitchen table who didn't know you'd come in. A parent at the hospital door.
A friend who says, I've been praying for you, and means it. You're hearing what they say about you to God. That's what the disciples get at this table.
Jesus prays for them out loud, while they sit right there. And what he asks is not what you might expect.

teach.b: He begins by describing them, and it's generous: they were yours, you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
These are the friends who argued about who was greatest, who missed half of what he said, one of whom will deny him tonight. He calls them faithful anyway.
Then the center of the prayer: "Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are." Keep.

teach.h: TEREO: TO GUARD, TO KEEP WATCH.
teach.b: The Greek is tereo: to watch over, to guard, the word for a guard keeping watch. While he was with them, he kept them himself. Now he's leaving, so he hands the job to the Father.
Then the line that surprises people: "I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil." He could have asked for an escape. He doesn't.

He wants them in the middle of things, guarded there. Some translations say from the evil one; the Greek can be read either way, and scholars differ. Then: "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth."
Sanctify means to set apart, make holy.

teach.h: NOT OUT OF THE WORLD, BUT KEPT.
teach.b: A few lines later: as you sent me into the world, so I've sent them into the world. Not out of it.
Christians often sum this up with a phrase drawn from these verses: in the world, but not of it.

how: Many Christians pray for friends and family by name every day, some with a written list, and intercession, praying for others, is part of almost every Christian service.

o: a prayer that God guard his friends where they are
a command to hold on to every law of Moses
a plea to lift his friends out of the world

games.q: what's inside John 17:6–19 — tap the pairs.

s: Jesus prays for his friends to be taken out of the world
"I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil."
the Greek can be read 'from evil' or 'from the evil one'
translations differ, and so do scholars.
the exact phrase 'in the world but not of it' appears in John 17
it's a summary Christians draw from these verses, not a quotation.

games.q: you're praying for friends you're about to leave behind in a dangerous place. what do you ask?
o: take them out of the world, somewhere safe.
keep them from evil, right where they are.
make them strong enough not to need anyone.
games.why: he asks for them to be kept, not removed: not out of the world, but kept from the evil.

practice: Bring three friends to mind, one at a time, and think of where each one is today: the job, the worry, the place they can't escape. Don't wish them out of it; wish them kept in it.
If you pray, say his words over each one by name, keep them; if not, hold each face for a few breaths and wish them safe where they are.

wordCard.voice: Keep them. Jesus asks the Father to guard his friends, not by taking them out of the world, but by keeping them safe in it.

orig.note: Greek: keep them. tereo means to watch over, to guard, to keep safe.

carryVoice: Your line: in the world, but not of it. Kept, not taken out. Day six hundred forty, done.
